comment: Table 1 (Summary statistics and T-tests, p. 117) prints only MEANS and MEDIANS - for the full sample and for both the CR and DSCR splits - with no standard deviation column. KDi,t (annual interest paid / total interest-bearing debt, INET BFA) has mean 9.5 and median 6.1 but no SD. The only standard deviation reported anywhere in the paper is for the carbon disclosure score.

COD decimal fraction (485 bp). Confidence low: the printed SD is 88% of the arithmetic maximum implied by the printed mean and range, which contradicts the interior median, and two other rows in the same table have outright impossible SDs.
CoD decimal fraction; SD consistent with the printed mean, range and median.

Table 2 Panel A (p. 6) prints Mean, Q1, Median and Q3 only - no SD column - for the full sample and both disclosure subsamples; the propensity-score-matching table (p. 8) reports means and differences only. The string 'standard deviation' does not occur anywhere in the paper. COBB (weighted average interest rate, full-sample mean 1.5174) therefore has no SD.
COD decimal fraction; SD arithmetically consistent but inflated by the winsorized right tail (max 2.613), so sd_bp 1220 is flagged. DeltaCOD is a change rate and gets no row.
Debt_Fcosts decimal fraction; SD consistent with both the printed range and the printed IQR.
Cost of debt(it+1) with '%' printed at the variable and restated in the text; SD consistent. Credit rating row not extracted.
Only Log (Spread) is tabulated with an SD. The text gives the raw-scale mean (172 bp) but no raw-scale SD, so no raw row could be created.

Table 3 (Descriptive Statistics, p. 8) prints Mean, Median, Minimum and Maximum only - no standard deviation column - although the methods text claims SD values are reported. Confirmed against the rendered page image. COD (mean 0.726, median 0.060, max 45.277) has no SD anywhere in the paper.

Two rows. CostDebt(t) converted to 1060 bp but confidence low: under the paper's stated 1% winsorization the printed mean and quartiles cap the SD at about 0.088, below the printed 0.106. Costdebt'(t) is the standardized version and is recorded with sd_bp empty - its SD of 1 is mechanical and carries no information.
LCOD is the log of CoD, and CoD is defined as Interest Expenses x (1 - Tax Rate) - a currency AMOUNT, not a rate. Not convertible to basis points under any factor; row recorded with sd_bp empty.
CD in percent (inferred from the range and corroborated by a 'CD (%)' column elsewhere in the paper); SD consistent.
Cost of Debt in percent (Bloomberg); SD consistent, though dispersion is near-uniform across the printed range.
Only Ln (cod) is tabulated. Back-transformation shows the underlying cod is scaled in basis points (exp(5.95) = 384 bp). SD consistent with both the printed range and the printed IQR.

The paper contains no descriptive statistics table: Table 1 is a correlation matrix and Tables 2-4 are regression output; Figure 1 shows annual mean levels of WACC and its components only. The string 'standard deviation' does not occur anywhere in the paper, so WACC Cost of Debt has no SD.

Cost of debt with '%' printed in the panel header; SD consistent. NON-INDEPENDENCE: this panel is numerically identical to Caragnano et al (2020) Table 2 Panel a - same sample, so the two studies are not independent observations.

Three rows, all SQUARE-ROOT transformed (sqrt_Debt Cost, sqrt_Short Term Debt Cost, sqrt_Long Term Debt Cost) - NOT logs. Status log_only is used because the vocabulary has no sqrt bucket and the operative fact is the same: only a transformed-scale SD exists, so no bp conversion is possible (squaring a mean recovers the raw scale, squaring an SD does not). All three SDs pass the arithmetic check.

Two rows, one per market subsample - Table 4 prints no pooled column. The variable definition's 'x100' implies percent but the printed values are decimal fractions; the paper's own trend table (3.96% developed, 4.99% emerging) settles it. Panels B and C are further cuts of the same firms and were not recorded separately.

The tabulated series is the log of CoD, and CoD is a currency amount (one minus tax rate into interest expenses) - not bp-convertible. NON-INDEPENDENCE: every statistic is numerically identical to Ofogbe et al (2021) Table 2; only the observation counts differ.
Table 3 (Descriptive analysis, p. 22518) prints N, Minimum, Maximum and Mean only - no standard deviation column. Cd (mean 7.19, range 1.52-12.59) has no SD anywhere in the paper.
Financing cost decimal fraction; SD consistent but printed to only 2 dp. The row labelled COD in the same table is Chemical Oxygen Demand, not cost of debt.
Cost decimal fraction; SD consistent with the printed range and median. Cost1 is not in the descriptives table.
COD decimal fraction, confirmed by percent equivalents in the text; SD consistent with the right-skewed range.

Two rows. COD converted at 10000 despite the text labelling it '%' - the literal reading would make it 6.1 bp, ninety times smaller than the paper's own alternative proxy. Interest converted at 100 as printed. Both SDs pass the arithmetic check.
COD decimal fraction, benchmarked in the text against Francis et al. (2005) and Pittman & Fortin (2004); SD consistent with the printed IQR but reported to only 2 dp.
Cost decimal fraction; SD consistent with the printed range and median.
COD decimal fraction; SD arithmetically consistent but dominated by a severe right tail (median 0.101 against a max of 4.781), so sd_bp 4830 is flagged.

Debtcost decimal fraction, confirmed in the text; SD arithmetically consistent but driven almost entirely by the upper tail (median 0.0049 against a mean of 0.0402 and a max of 0.6680), so sd_bp 1050 is flagged.
COD decimal fraction; SD arithmetically consistent but dominated by the right tail (median 0.0800 against a mean of 0.220), so sd_bp 3300 is flagged.
COD decimal fraction, confirmed by the text ('Cost of debt ranges from 0 % to 18.9 %'); SD consistent. data_basis unknown - the paper does not name its data source.

COD (interest paid / total debt) appears only in the regression tables (Tables 6-10) and in the text. None of the paper's three summary-statistics tables - Table 1 CSR scores (p. 10), Table 2 executive characteristics (p. 14), Table 3 board and firm variables (p. 15) - nor Appendix A includes COD; no mean or SD for COD is printed anywhere. RATE and GRADE in Table 3 are credit-rating variables, which are never extracted.

COD decimal fraction, but the printed SD (2.887) is roughly 33x the arithmetic maximum implied by the printed mean, min and max - IMPOSSIBLE, not merely implausible. A second row in the same table (ROA) is impossible too. Recorded unrepaired at 28,870 bp, flagged, confidence low. Do not use without a corrected table.
Loan spreads (all-in-drawn) in basis points; SD consistent with the printed 5th/50th/95th percentiles.
COST (interest expenses / total loan) decimal fraction; SD consistent with both the printed range and the printed IQR.
